text: Follow the Starlight.
Which light is a star?
Ari knows three lights from their first journey. Dot finds one light that makes its own glow.
Planets shine with sunlight. Stars make their own light.
Unknown light found. Mission accepted!
Which point is our Sun from far away?
From far away, even our enormous Sun becomes one tiny point among the others.
There is no visual clue. Our Sun is a star that looks big because it is close.
What keeps a star steady?
Gravity pulls inward. Pressure from the hot core pushes outward. A steady star needs both.
Gravity pulls in. Pressure from the hot core pushes out. A steady star needs both.
Which star is our middle-sized Sun?
Stars come in many sizes. Our Sun sits between tiny red dwarfs and enormous giants.
This is our Sun. Some stars are much smaller, and some are hundreds of times wider.
Which star is hottest?
Star colour is evidence. Blue-white stars are hotter than red stars—the opposite of many taps.
Blue-white stars are hotter than red stars.
Look again.
That is it.
Venus is the brightest planet in the night sky.
Mars looks red because its dust is rusty.
Jupiter is about 11 Earths wide.
Planets shine with the Sun's light. Stars make their own.
Diameter: about 1.39 million km (about 109 Earths wide)
Surface temperature: about 5,500°C
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
The next-closest star is about 40 trillion km away.
Its light takes about 4 years to reach us.
Core temperature: about 15 million°C
Surface temperature: about 5,500°C
Stars are mostly hydrogen and helium gas.
The Sun has been shining for about 4.6 billion years.
The Sun's gravity helps keep the solar system together.
Red dwarfs are the most common stars of all.
Diameter: about 1.39 million km (about 109 Earths wide)
Arcturus, a giant, is about 25 times wider than the Sun.
Betelgeuse, a supergiant, is hundreds of times wider than the Sun.
A red dwarf can shine for trillions of years.
Blue-white stars are the hottest: over 10,000°C.
Our Sun is yellow-white: about 5,500°C
Red stars are the coolest: about 3,000°C.
Betelgeuse looks red-orange. About 3,300°C.
Rigel looks blue-white. About 12,000°C.
Why can two stars look equally bright?
A star can look bright because it makes a lot of light, or because it is close. Appearance alone cannot tell us which.
Both can happen. Brightness depends on a star's true power and its distance.
Sirius is the brightest star in our night sky.
Sirius is close: about 8.6 light-years.
Sirius is about 25 times brighter than the Sun.
Rigel is about 120,000 times brighter than the Sun, about 860 light-years away.
Twice as far looks four times dimmer.
Which journey is 268,000 Sun-steps?
If Earth to the Sun were one step, Neptune would be thirty steps away. The nearest star would be about 268,000 steps.
The nearest star is about 268,000 Earth-to-Sun distances away.
Earth to the Sun is about 150 million kilometres.
Neptune is about 4.5 billion kilometres from the Sun.
Proxima Centauri is about 40 trillion kilometres away.
Proxima Centauri is about 268,000 times the Earth-Sun distance.
Voyager 1 would need about 75,000 years.
Which is a distance?
Light is fast, but not instant. A light-year is a distance: how far light travels in one whole year.
A light-year is a distance, not an amount of time.
Light travels about 300,000 kilometres every second.
Moonlight takes about 1.3 seconds.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds.
A light-year is about 9.46 trillion kilometres.
Proxima's light left about 4.2 years ago.
Which picture uses these same seven stars?
The stars are real. The joining lines are pictures people invented to remember the sky.
The Big Dipper joins these seven stars without moving any of them.
There are 88 official constellations.
The Big Dipper's seven stars are part of the Great Bear.
It is called the Plough in Britain and the Big Dipper in North America.
Two Dipper stars point to Polaris.
Ptolemy listed 48 constellations about 1,900 years ago.
From where does the Dipper shape line up?
Constellation stars can be very far apart in depth. From another viewpoint, their picture falls apart.
From Earth, different-depth stars line up as the familiar Dipper.
Dipper stars are about 80 to 125 light-years away.
Their light left 80 to 125 years ago.
In about 100,000 years the Dipper will look different.
From another star the sky's pictures would look different.
They are neighbours in the sky, not in space.
Which cloud can make a star?
Stars begin in huge, cold clouds of gas and dust. Gravity gathers part of a cloud into a denser clump.
A dense clump gives gravity enough material to begin making a star.
A glowing cloud of gas and dust is a nebula.
A star-forming cloud is about minus 260 degrees Celsius.
A star-forming cloud is about 99 percent gas and 1 percent dust.
The Orion Nebula is a star nursery about 1,350 light-years away.
The Sun was born in a cloud about 4.6 billion years ago.
What makes the centre light?
Gravity pulls gas inward. The centre heats, and at about ten million degrees it ignites as a star.
Gravity squeezes the gas. Compression heats it until fusion begins.
The middle must reach about 10 million degrees Celsius.
A Sun-like star takes tens of millions of years to form.
A bicycle pump gets warm because compressing gas heats it.
An unlit star is a protostar.
Once lit, a star turns hydrogen into helium.
Where is the Sun now?
Our Sun is about 4.6 billion years into a roughly 10-billion-year stable stage.
The Sun is about halfway through its long, steady stage.
The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old.
The Sun's steady stage lasts about 10 billion years.
The Sun turns about 4 million tonnes of matter into energy every second.
The Sun's brightness changes by about 0.1 percent in its 11-year cycle.
A red dwarf stays steady for trillions of years.
Which planets are swallowed by the red giant?
Very far in the future, the Sun will become a red giant and expand beyond Mercury and Venus.
Mercury and Venus are engulfed. Earth's fate is still uncertain.
In about 5 billion years the Sun swells into a red giant.
The red-giant Sun will be more than 100 times wider.
Its surface will be about 3,000 degrees Celsius, so it looks red.
Mercury and Venus will be swallowed.
Five billion years is about 16,000 times human history.
What remains after the outer gas drifts away?
A Sun-like star releases its outer layers into a glowing ring and leaves an Earth-sized white dwarf.
A Sun-like star leaves a white dwarf, not a black hole.
A planetary nebula has nothing to do with planets.
A white dwarf is about Earth-sized, roughly 12,700 kilometres wide.
A new white dwarf is over 100,000 degrees Celsius.
The Ring Nebula is about 2,000 light-years away.
The universe is 13.8 billion years old, and no white dwarf has gone dark.
Which star dies first?
Massive stars own more fuel, but use it so quickly that they live much shorter lives.
The massive star dies first because it burns fuel enormously faster.
The Sun lives about 10 billion years.
A star 10 times heavier lives tens of millions of years.
A red dwarf lives trillions of years.
No red dwarf has died yet; the universe is 13.8 billion years old.
The heaviest stars are over 100 Suns.
Which star can explode as a supernova?
When a massive star runs out of fuel, its core collapses and the outer star bursts into space.
A star more than about eight Suns heavy can end in a core-collapse supernova.
A core-collapse supernova needs a star more than about 8 Suns heavy.
Its core collapses in less than a second.
A supernova can shine as bright as a whole galaxy for weeks.
Supernova debris moves about 10,000 kilometres per second.
The 1054 supernova was seen in daylight; the Crab Nebula is its remains.
What can our Sun become?
Most stars leave white dwarfs. Heavier stars can leave neutron stars or black holes.
Our Sun will become a white dwarf.
Stars up to about 8 Suns leave a white dwarf.
A neutron star is about 20 kilometres wide and heavier than the Sun.
A sugar cube of neutron-star matter would weigh about a billion tonnes.
Black holes can come from stars over about 20 Suns.
The Sun will become a white dwarf.
Where is our Sun?
The Milky Way holds at least 100 billion stars. Our Sun sits away from the centre in one spiral arm.
Our Sun is in one spiral arm, about 26,000 light-years from the centre.
The Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across.
The Milky Way has at least 100 billion stars.
The Sun is about 26,000 light-years from the centre.
The Sun takes about 230 million years to orbit the galaxy.
Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away.
Which star has a planet?
When a planet crosses its star, it blocks a tiny amount of light. The dip repeats each orbit.
The repeated clean dip matches a planet crossing its star.
New mission accepted.
A planet crossing its star is a transit.
Jupiter-size blocks about 1 percent; Earth-size about 0.01 percent.
Kepler, launched in 2009, found more than 2,600 planets.
TESS, launched in 2018, watches stars near us.
Over 6,000 planets are known.
